newsitem.title: UK: UK opinion polls send mixed messages.
newsitem.headline: UK opinion polls send mixed messages.

text.p: Prime Minister John Major's Conservatives took heart from an opinion poll to be published on Thursday showing a significant erosion of Labour's lead ahead of Britain's general election on May 1.
But another poll suggested that Labour had widened its lead and was heading for a landslide victory.
A MORI poll for The Times showed a six point rise in Conservative support to 34 percent and a six point fall for Labour to 49 percent, with the Liberal Democrats on 12 percent.

Major told reporters the reduction in Labour's lead to 15 points, compared with 27 points last week, indicated that the election campaign was finally taking off, with voters focussing on issues rather than so-called "sleaze" stories.
Party officials said the Conservatives also drew comfort from a Gallup poll for Channel 4 television news which said 50 percent of voters were not firmly committed to voting for one party or another.
The poll gave Labour 54 percent support, the Conservatives 31 percent and the Liberal Democrats 10 percent.
But the Labour lead dropped to 14 points when people who were not certain to vote, those who might switch their vote and those with no history of vote switching were excluded.

A Gallup poll for Thursday's Daily Telegraph gave Labour 53 percent, the Conservatives 30 percent and the Liberal Democrats 11 percent. It said Labour's lead had widened to 23 points from 19 points last Wednesday.
"Key to the Tories' (Conservatives') inability to make consistent inroads on the Labour lead is the issue of trust," The Telegraph said.
"Attempts by the Tories to show the Labour Party are shifting their ground on policy issues such as privatisation seem to be backfiring."
